# ESGenius: Benchmarking LLMs on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and Sustainability Knowledge

Chaoyue He1Xin Zhou1 \*Yi Wu1Xinjia $\mathbf { V } \mathbf { u } ^ { 1 }$ Yan Zhang1 Lei Zhang1   
Di WanglShengfei LyulHong $\mathbf { X } \mathbf { u } ^ { 1 }$ Xiaoqiao Wang²Wei Liu2 Chunyan Miaol   
1Alibaba-NTU Global e-Sustainability CorpLab (ANGEL), Singapore; ²Alibaba Group, China {cyhe，xin.zhou，xinjia.yu， zhang.yan}@ntu.edu.sg {wangdi， shengfei.lyu， xuhong，ascymiao}@ntu.edu.sg {wuyi0614，leizhanzzl.1103}@gmail.com {nerissa.wxq，weiliu.liuwei}@alibaba-inc.com GitHub: https://github.com/ANGEL-NTU/ESGenius Web Portal: https: //angel-ntu.github.io/ESGenius

![](images/e1b13ee38d0a4987201b4ddc25e51a14fc03495bac63358791893eadd28b11bb.jpg)  
Figure 1: The ESGenius pipeline for benchmark creation and model evaluation. The process begins with the ESGenius-Corpus,a curated collction of 231 authoritative PDFs from7key ESG sources.Text is extracted from these documents and used in an LLM-driven pipeline to generate candidate MCQs. These questions then undergo rigorous validation by domain experts to produce the final ESGenius-QA dataset, which contains 1136 high-quality MCQs (An example question is shown above).Finally,this dataset is used to benchmark 50 diffrent LLMs from 5 renowned families, with sizes ranging from 0.5B to 671B parameters, via open-source models (OSS)or proprietary APIs.The evaluation is performed in two setings: a zero-shot setup to test the models' inherent ESG knowledge and a RAG setup to assess their ability to synthesize information from the source documents.
